w10_P4_000548: A laboratory report ends with a value that is 5 times a site figure, because 5 laboratories report together. Each site figure is what you get by adding a standing instrument allowance of 29 kJ to a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy a glider of 38 kg carries because of its motion along the air track, and the glider's speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 10x + 24 = 0. The track is 2 m long, a dimension the report never uses. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?
w10_P4_000561: A launch bench brings a carriage of 31 kg up to speed along a level rail, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 5t^2 + 7t, with t the time in seconds. Between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval, and the speed reached at the end is the launch speed. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at that speed and expresses it in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 3 for the 3 carriages in a run, by 7 for the 7 runs in a session, and by 2 for the 2 sessions in the study. The rail is 25 m long, a length the bench never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000562: A machine-shop ledger closes with a number that is 16 kN more than a figure, and that figure is 8 times an adjusted reading, since 8 slides run together. The adjusted reading is what you get by adding a fixed mounting allowance of 30 kN to a converted force. That converted force is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a tool head of 34000 grams, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is the rate at which the slope of the fitted position curve 5x^3 + 0x^2 is itself changing at the instant x = 2 seconds, with x the time in seconds and the position in metres. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the ledger?
w10_P4_000564: A calibration rig holds 13 identical reference masses, and the acceleration it applies, in metres per second squared, is the number of distinct pairs that can be chosen from them. That acceleration is given to a shuttle of 5000 grams on the rig's rail. The controller records the force needed to drive the shuttle and multiplies it by 3, because the routine runs on 3 axes, then expresses the result in kilonewtons. A fixed frame allowance of 21 kN is added to the converted figure, and the sum is multiplied by 2 because two rigs run the routine together. What number, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000565: A press bench accelerates a tool head of 175 kg along its slide. The head's position in metres is modelled by the fitted curve 3x^3 + 0x^2, with x the time in seconds, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing at the instant x = 2 seconds. The controller works out the force needed for that acceleration and subtracts a bearing tare of 23 N. The remainder is multiplied by 11 for the 11 heads on the machine and then by 5 for the 5 machines in the shop. The slide is 3 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000566: A test plant keeps 10 identical reference masses, and the acceleration its rig applies, in metres per second squared, is the number of distinct pairs that can be chosen from them. The controller records the force needed to drive the carrier, multiplies it by 4 because 4 carriers run together, and expresses the result in kilonewtons. The converted figure is then multiplied by 12 for the 12 rigs in the plant, and a fixed frame allowance of 3 kN is added at the end. The plant floor is 30 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000568: A test-bed ledger closes with a number that is 15 kN more than a figure from which a contractual credit of 8 kN had already been subtracted. w10_P4_000570: A gantry report ends with a number found by taking a contractual credit of 25 kN off a converted total. That converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure that is 11 times a single-carriage value, since 11 carriages run on the beam. w10_P4_000571: A conveyor drive accelerates a crate of 46000 grams along the rollers, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 8. w10_P4_000575: A test bench drives a slide of 110000 grams, and the rate at which its acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 4t^2 + 8t. w10_P4_000576: A teaching bench releases a glider of 38000 grams along a level air track. w10_P4_000578: A plant figure is 5 times a hall total, because 5 halls run the same job, and each hall total is 11 times a converted machine reading. w10_P4_000580: A gantry drives a carriage of 79000 grams along its beam, and the carriage's position in metres is modelled by the fitted curve 2x^3 + 2x^2, with x the time in seconds. w10_P4_000595: A yard report ends with a number that is 8 times a depot figure, because 8 depots report together. Each depot figure is 3 times a converted reading, since 3 tugs work at a depot. w10_P4_000607: A test report ends with a figure that is 3 times the energy of a single launch, because 3 launches make a set. w10_P4_000614: A crash-test facility launches a trolley of 25000 grams along a straight track. The trolley's launch speed in metres per second is 4 times the sum of 9 and 10. w10_P4_000618: A depot report ends with a number that is 5 times a converted total, because 5 depots report together.
